newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Monday, November 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Monday, November 18.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
* In a letter to Prime minister former magistrate and Public Works minister Antonio Di Pietro confirmed he is not going back on his decision to resign (all).
* The centre-right announced it is refusing to participate in the parliamentary debate over the 1997 budget not only in the Lower House but also in the Upper House (all).

* Cuban leader Fidel Castro took centre stage again on the closing day of Rome's World food summit and went to dinner with Fiat honorary chairman Giovanni Agnelli. Castro is expected to pay a historic visit to the Pope tomorrow (all). ----------
* The government and the three main trade unions are expected to meet today to discuss the Euro-tax and the labour pact signed in September.

* In an interview, Industry minister Pier Luigi Bersani says state industrial holding Iri after the planned merger between Stet and Telecom Italia will have "a huge task: restore to health and privatise all the remaining assets, from Alitalia to Finmeccanica". Bersani also says the government might decide to open talks over the highly controversial telecom sector's reform (Repubblica).
* State-controlled Banca nazionale del Lavoro and insurer Ina are expected to join forces and declare today a preliminary interest in the sale of loss-making Banco di Napoli (Repubblica).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
